pinboard.title: Jensen Huang said to have had relationship with Nvidia executive who reports to him • The New York Times
pinboard.description:
Ryan Mac, Tripp Mickle and Georgia Gee:

Jensen Huang, the leader of Nvidia who is under investigation for an affair with a woman who US intelligence determined is a Chinese spy, also had an extramarital relationship with an executive who reports to him, according to five people who worked at the company. The relationship, which has not been previously reported, was with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care, said the people, who spoke under the condition of anonymity to describe sensitive information. Under Nvidia’s code of conduct, employees are told to “avoid situations where our actions create conflict” including “personal relationships,” and the company states that it “promptly investigates reports of misconduct.” Many corporations have policies against managers having relationships with subordinates. Mr. Huang, 63, and Ms. Powell, 48, were captured on video being affectionate at a San Jose, Calif., hotel during a Nvidia conference in March, according to two of the people who worked at the company. The New York Times has not seen the video. Both Mr. Huang and Ms. Powell are married to other people.

The NY Times is going to pick away at this story endlessly, because it knows there's a goldmine. Meanwhile, Nvidia starts to look less like a well-run company and more like one guy's personal fiefdom. (The WSJ suggests that the board will try to force him out.)

pinboard.description:
Saul Cornell, a Second Amendment scholar and history professor at Fordham University, said relying on centuries-old legal precedents requires understanding how earlier generations used language. He said “dangerous and unusual” is most likely an example of hendiadys, in which a single concept is expressed in multiple words connected by “and.” One famous example of hendiadys is Shakespeare’s “full of sound and fury,” which meant furious sound.

“The best translation of Blackstone’s terminology,” Dr. Cornell said, “would be to treat ‘dangerous and unusual’ as a synonym for unusually dangerous.”

pinboard.title: Opinion | I Am a Silicon Valley Veteran. We Are Sabotaging Ourselves. - The New York Times
pinboard.description:
By Jaron Lanier
There are better alternatives to agents. I do research into complex new manufacturing and materials technology using large A.I. models. In the course of my efforts, I am pelted with pop-ups to launch agents, but I have realized they are not so effective because I have to constantly backpedal when I get results that aren’t quite right — unless I give in and accept what comes easy to the agent. (This is how A.I. slop happens.) Instead, I am starting to use a process I call Mind Gliders, where I use the newest models to create a custom, single-use editor for the general zone of ideas I want to research at that moment, and then explore possibilities using sliders on my screen until I have zeroed in on what I was trying to create.

pinboard.title: What is AWS Emulator? - AWS Emulator
pinboard.description:
AWS Emulator is a local emulator of the AWS APIs. You use it to test your software without calling AWS, on your own machine, on a development server, or in continuous integration (CI). You don’t need an AWS account. Your requests go to the emulator, not to AWS. So you work with emulated resources instead of AWS resources. AWS Emulator has no additional service fee. You pay only for AWS resources when you deploy on AWS.

The emulator is a local program that serves an AWS API endpoint. It has no graphical interface. After you start the emulator, you set environment variables to point the AWS CLI or an AWS SDK at its endpoint. Then you run your code as usual. In embedded mode, you pass the emulator’s HTTP client to your SDK instead.

The emulator doesn’t send your requests, responses, or resource data to AWS. By default, it sends anonymous usage and error data, which you can turn off. For more information, see Telemetry in AWS Emulator.

On Linux, you install AWS Emulator from an RPM or Debian package for x86_64 or aarch64, and run it as a command-line tool. On macOS and Windows, you run it in Docker, from an image that you build with our Dockerfile. For tests written in Rust with the AWS SDK for Rust, you can also run the emulator inside your test process. For more information, see Getting started with AWS Emulator.

pinboard.title: lo-pi radio
pinboard.description:
This station will remain on-air until the collapse of humanity, or we stop paying our web-hosting bill. Whichever comes first.

Created by Russell Samora and Kevin Litman-Navarro for The Pudding.

This is a companion piece to our main story The Afterlife of Pi. Read more to learn about the history of its calculation and the unexpected paths it took across a century.

How the sound works: Every note of the melody you hear is the next digit of pi, in order. Each digit is a note in the Fmaj scale. 0 and 9 are rests (silence). Digits are not skipped or changed, but we've created a set of simple rules (and some fiddly ones that aren't worth explaining) that decide when each note plays and how long it lasts to best match the underlying progression.

pinboard.title: AI is history | Brendan Keogh
pinboard.description: But I’m always deeply suspicious of any attempt to situate a technology outside of history. My whole academic career to date has, in part, been about resisting narratives of videogames as magically totally different from every media form that came before them. I am likewise skeptical that generative AI represents a profound cut from history. That somehow, unlike every previous contradictory technological innovation of the past couple centuries of capitalism, generative AI is just simply ‘evil’. Instead, I would suggest it represents the same profound contradictions of technological innovation under capitalism as all the previous ones, just now on an even larger scale. The potentially useful byproducts are larger, as is the possible profits that are the actual goal and the undeniable harms.
